messages:
samir: proposal: add optional `signed_confidence` and `model_hint` to /v1/rerank responses. also suggest a 'partial' flag when we backpressure and return top-k early. intent is to make downstream blending and telemetry easier without breaking old clients. thoughts?
elaine: curious — is `signed_confidence` required for billing/scoring? is this purely for provenance or do we want clients to rely on it?
samir: not required. it's opt-in. idea: signed_confidence is an int16 scaled value + sig over (score, model_id, ts) so we can detect weird regressions and attribute to model variant. docs will say never use as absolute probability for biz logic.
rasheed: backpressure/limits question: if we return partial results (partial=true) should we charge full unit for the requested fanout or only for items actually scored? ops wants clear billing rules.
maria: from console/telemetry POV we should surface both: requested_candidates, scored_candidates, and fallback_reason. console toggle to show 'requested vs charged' so folks can reconcile.
jordan: for model selection, propose we accept `model_affinity: ["m1","m2"]` in request and runtime tries in order with fast-fail fallback. if only a cheaper model responds with partial=true we should include `fallback_trace` in response.
samir: agreed on affinity list. also propose server returns `score_units_consumed` and `score_unit_version` in envelope for billing parity.
elaine: compatibility: how do older clients handle extra fields? we must ensure SDKs ignore unknown fields and typed clients get updated. also deprecation window?
samir: deprecate nothing. fields are optional. SDKs will add convenience helpers.
rasheed: on throttling semantics: new proposal: when capacity constrained, return 429 vs return 200 with partial=true? ops prefers 200+partial for graceful degradation of user UX, but platform metrics become trickier.
maria: console needs an explicit metric for partial responses so we can surface health per-model and per-tenant. if we use 200 for partial it needs a distinct telemetry tag: `rerank.partial=true`.
jordan: can we include a hint `retry_in_ms` when we do partial so clients can decide to requeue?
samir: yes — include `retry_hint_ms` optional. also include `fanout_requested` and `fanout_scored`.
elaine: example payload?
samir: paste: ```json
{
  "candidates": [{"id":"u1","score":0.87}],
  "model_id":"re-rank-v3",
  "signed_confidence":"v1:abc123",
  "model_hint":"re-rank-v3-quant",
  "partial": true,
  "fallback_trace": ["model_timeout","affinity_fallback:m2"],
  "fanout_requested": 100,
  "fanout_scored": 24,
  "score_units_consumed": 24,
  "retry_hint_ms": 250,
  "tags": ["rerank.partial","tenant:acme"]
}
```
rasheed: ops question: does `score_units_consumed` map 1:1 to billing? if we have KV cache hits should we bill less?
samir: yes we bill consumed units. cache hits reduce computation and thus units. will update billing doc.
maria: console UX: add an on-by-default checkbox "Show partial responses" on rerank route dashboard. also a histogram of fanout_requested vs fanout_scored. product wants a rollout with a small canary first.
jordan: rollout plan: feature-flag the signed_confidence + partial flag server-side. default off for tenants with existing canary group. enable telemetry in canary, run 2 weeks. escalate if partial>10% or cost delta > 8%.
samir: sounds good. can we standardize the `fallback_trace` enums? we should list: model_timeout, capacity_limit, affinity_fallback, kv_cache_hit, latency_shed.
elaine: please add a schema PR for the protos and update openapi. i'll coordinate SDK changes once schema PR lands.
samir: i'll open the schema PR. action items: @samir open schema PR, @maria add console toggle + histogram draft, @rasheed confirm billing mapping for cached vs computed units, @jordan prepare canary flags and rollout playbook.
ops-bot: CI: rerank-schema-tests passed (link: https://ci.redwood/proj/3421) :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary flag created: rerank.partial.toggle (env: canary).
samir: thanks all — let's reconvene after schema PR review. :thumbsup:
